actual_encoder_run.latency_method: Monotonic wall clock. Median and nearest-rank p95 over 18 queries. For this sample count p95 equals the observed maximum. Cold query timings exclude encoder loading and warmup. Core.process includes its normal 200ms coalescing wait.

failure_injection_method.timeout: The loopback handler delayed the same genuine encoder response by two seconds. query_options returned lexical fallback at the 1.5-second deadline.
failure_injection_method.dimensions: The real encoder returned 512 values while HTTPEmbedding expected 513. The response was rejected.
failure_injection_method.model_version: A genuine query vector was retrieved with a deliberately different index-version identifier. Retrieval matched the lexical baseline.

reproduction.prerequisites: Use an isolated checkout matching the recorded source hashes, its Python 3.13 application environment, and an existing compatible Python 3.11 torch/transformers environment. The run used existing dependencies.
steps: Create a dedicated temporary workspace and set ELEPHANT_REPO to the isolated repository checkout. Run application scripts from the repository working directory so the default persona path resolves.
Write dataset.json from the embedded dataset using the recorded UTF-8 formatting, verify dataset_sha256, and write that hash followed by a newline to dataset.sha256.

Restore the portable scripts below by joining each lines array with newline and adding a trailing newline. Keep encoder_server.py and run_evaluation.py at the temporary workspace root, and the replay script in postfix-context-replay/.
Download the six public model files from encoder.files into workspace/model/ using curl with TLS verification. Verify every byte length and SHA-256. Save the encoder metadata as model-manifest.json.

For the historical before-fix phase, match actual_encoder_run_source_sha256. Start encoder_server.py with the existing encoder interpreter and HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1, TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false. Wait for ready.json.

Run run_evaluation.py with the repository Python 3.13 interpreter. It creates an isolated synthetic DB, indexes source-backed records, performs the explicit correction, compares lexical/hybrid retrieval, measures normal Core.process seed consumption, and writes raw traces and metrics.
Stop the PID recorded in ready.json with SIGTERM after evaluation. Confirm its loopback port closed, then remove workspace/model/. Keep hashes and synthetic traces.

For after-fix context replay, use the serialization_fix_source_sha256 snapshot, the generated synthetic DB and saved real ranking. Run postfix-context-replay/replay.py with the application interpreter. The replay uses saved ranking with fresh source visibility checks and performs zero new embedding inference.

Keep the frozen relevance labels and report any changed or failed result. Different runtime builds and hardware may change floating-point hashes and latency. Reproduction should report measured outcomes.

limitations: The corpus and 18 relevance expectations are handcrafted synthetic examples, with one expected memory per query. They are a small functional evaluation.
The real encoder was BAAI CPU inference on this macOS host. Home embedding service configuration and online supplier latency remain separate acceptance work.
Synthetic adapter capability state and local Core.process context creation were exercised. QQ transport and final generated answers were outside this run.
The original zero-character-overlap subset retained one top-five miss. The vegetarian target remains rank seven after serialization repair.
The later serialization replay reused actual ranking and stored source vectors. Its full-seed coverage is a context-retention result and adds no new model-quality measurement.
The runtime was an existing development build of torch. Exact package versions, source fingerprints, method and public model-file hashes are recorded for interpreting reproduction differences.
